A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProSec research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V2 reports original security-alignment experiments, multilingual code-generation evaluations, ablations, and comparisons of preference objectives.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds iterative-refinement comparisons, dataset controls, and experiments on three additional models.

M1.justification: The instruction synthesis, repair-based preference construction, utility-preservation data, heuristic filtering, and training-dynamics selection procedures remain unchanged. Figure 1 corrects the displayed normal/fixed-code preference order to match the definition already given in v2 Section 3.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use Infinity-Instruct, PurpleLlama’s 38 language/CWE pairs with 694 test cases, HumanEval-Multi, and MXEval. Additional model experiments retain this coverage. Newly cited CodeLMSec is discussed as related work, not evaluated.

E2.justification: V3 adds static-analyzer-guided iterative refinement as a comparator in Table 4 and SafeCoder augmented with Dnorm in Table 5. The main SafeCoder and SafeCoder-Inst comparisons remain. Table 2’s change from Select to ProSec is only renaming.

E3.justification: V2 Table 4 specifies 1,500 SimPO steps; v3 Table 6 specifies 1,500 for Phi3/Phi4-mini and 400 for other models, changing the reported CodeLlama setting. V3 also adds three model configurations, refinement limits of 3/5/10 iterations, and size-matched and mixed-dataset controls. These substantially extend the evaluation design without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 Table 5 adds direct tests of dataset-size confounding and the effect of adding Dnorm to SafeCoder. Table 4 tests security sensitivity to refinement budgets. These address additional explanatory questions beyond the retained instruction-synthesis, clustering, sampling, training-dynamics, and preference-objective analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-training-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Multiple generated completions and training-checkpoint analyses are retained procedures, not newly added uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the ProSec CodeLlama results: average vulnerability changes from 3.46% to 26.04%, HumanEval-Multi from 25.14% to 29.02%, and MXEval from 36.18% to 39.89%, alongside a changed training budget. V3 Tables 4–5 add refinement and dataset-control results. Table 7 adds three models; its Phi4 comparison shows small utility declines after alignment despite improved security.

T1.justification: The formal datasets, static-analyzer abstraction, preference objective, and training-dynamics equations remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the claimed security improvement over SafeCoder from 25.2%–91.4% to 25.2%–35.4%, matching the revised results. The principal contributions, 25-fold vulnerability-induction claim, sevenfold dataset-size claim, and utility-preservation claim remain.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the size-matched control as supporting a data-quality advantage beyond dataset quantity. It adds inference-cost and latency arguments for iterative refinement, and Appendix A discusses agents catching alignment’s uncovered edge cases. Existing offline-training, reasoning, and preference-objective limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V3 newly discloses synthesizing 10,000 instructions per CWE, selecting 2,000 through clustering, and approximately $5 synthesis cost per CWE. Appendix C updates training schedules and revises the hardware disclosure from eight A100-40G GPUs for all experiments to two for ProSec training. The code/data repository reference changes from prosec-authors/prosec to PurCL/ProSec.

R1.justification: V3 expands research positioning through a new discussion of code-analysis agents and their complementarity with alignment, additional static-analysis references, and an explicit distinction between security benchmarks such as CodeLMSec and alignment datasets. Existing security-hardening and training-dynamics discussions are retained and moved into Section 7.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized prose and heading edits, moves existing related-work passages from Appendix A into Section 7, inserts the model-generalization subsection, and adds acknowledgements. Most methodological prose and the overall narrative structure remain stable.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 4, 5, and 7, restructures the hyperparameter table, and highlights ProSec rows in blue. Figure 1 corrects the preference-order display; Figures 3–4 are resized and appendix prompt figures are repacked. Existing figures and preference-objective results remain despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens empirical support through the size-matched and Dnorm controls in Table 5 and broader model validation in Table 7, while improving implementation documentation. The smaller CodeLlama security gain accompanies a changed training budget and higher reported utility, so it is not a same-setting regression. These useful gains are tempered by absent uncertainty estimates and the unqualified utility-preservation claim despite small Phi4 utility declines.
